judgments.title: Licensee Has No Reporting or Accounting Obligations
judgments.reason: The absence of reporting and accounting obligations is a substantive contractual omission rather than a construction risk.

judgments.title: Licensor Best Efforts Standard May Be Insufficient
judgments.reason: The phrase “would be reasonably likely to affect” leaves a fact-sensitive threshold for when Licensee's step-in right arises and therefore presents some vagueness risk.

judgments.title: Mandatory Consent to All Registration Requests
judgments.reason: “Licensor shall consent to any request” is mandatory and textually clear; the lack of discretion is a substantive negotiation concern.

judgments.title: No Licensee Obligation to Actively Develop or Operate
judgments.reason: The absence of an active-development or minimum-use covenant is a contractual omission, not an ambiguity or internal inconsistency.

judgments.title: Best Efforts Standard for Trademark Registrations
judgments.reason: “Best efforts” does not specify concrete trademark-maintenance actions or limits and therefore presents some vagueness regarding the required performance.

judgments.title: Costs of Remedial Trademark Filings Not Allocated
judgments.reason: Silence concerning the costs of Licensee's remedial filings is an omitted allocation term, not a contradiction or intrinsic textual defect.

judgments.title: Broad Prohibition on Internet Merchandise Sales
judgments.reason: The Internet-merchandise restrictions and channel separation are express and coherent; the issue concerns commercial flexibility rather than construction.

judgments.title: Mail Order Prohibition Overly Restrictive
judgments.reason: The mail-order prohibition is explicit; its restrictiveness and lack of a requested exception are negotiation issues.

judgments.title: Licensor's Standalone Merchandise Restriction Too Narrow
judgments.reason: The condition requiring both specified facilities is textually clear; the resulting commercial carve-out is not a construction defect.

judgments.title: Internet Sales Channel Creates Unrestricted Global Reach
judgments.reason: Section 2(b)(v) authorizes a sales channel but does not expressly override Section 2(a)'s territorial limitation, so the provisions can be harmonized without a genuine conflict.

judgments.title: Exhibit E Designations Subject to Permanent Cessation

judgments.title: No Consent Requirement for Assignment by Licensee
judgments.reason: The issue identifies the absence of an assignment-consent restriction, which is a negotiation gap rather than ambiguity or conflict.

judgments.title: All Goodwill Inures Solely to Licensor
judgments.reason: The phrase “all associated goodwill generated thereby” can reasonably raise a scope question as to whether it covers only goodwill in the licensed marks or broader goodwill generated by Licensee's operations.

judgments.title: No Right to Approve Licensed Products Before Sale
judgments.reason: Section 4(c)'s inspection-related sample obligation is clear; the absence of a pre-sale approval right is a commercial omission.

judgments.title: Undefined term: License Agreements

judgments.title: Arbitration Costs Not Shifted to Losing Party
judgments.reason: Equal sharing of arbitration fees and costs is unambiguous, and the absence of prevailing-party cost shifting creates no construction defect.

judgments.title: Arbitration Costs Shared Equally
judgments.reason: Mandatory equal cost sharing is clear, and replacing it with loser-pays allocation would change the bargain rather than resolve a construction defect.

judgments.title: Licensor Has Full Control of Joint Proceedings
judgments.reason: Licensor's control of joint proceedings and equal cost sharing are clearly stated; the absence of Licensee consent rights is a commercial concern only.

judgments.title: One-Sided Indemnification
judgments.reason: The issue concerns commercial asymmetry and the absence of reciprocal indemnification, not ambiguity, mechanical error, or conflict within the agreement.

judgments.title: Indemnification Lacks Defense Procedure and Cost Allocation
judgments.reason: The omission of express attorneys' fees and detailed defense procedures concerns the desired scope of protection, not ambiguity or inconsistency identified by the issue.

judgments.title: First Offer Right Triggered Too Broadly
judgments.reason: The trigger “all or substantially all of his assets and/or rights in connection with” has uncertain boundaries, particularly regarding reorganizations and partial or affiliated transfers.

judgments.title: Weak First Offer Rights — No Matching Right
judgments.reason: The clause clearly provides only negotiation rights and permits a later third-party transaction; the absence of a matching right is not a construction defect.

judgments.title: Perpetual Non-Attack Obligation
judgments.reason: The perpetual non-attack obligation is substantively broad but textually clear; the absence of requested carve-outs is a negotiation issue.

judgments.title: Injunctive Relief Without Bond Primarily Favors Licensor
judgments.reason: The differing scope of the parties' injunctive-relief rights is explicit rather than ambiguous or internally contradictory.

judgments.title: Licensee's Injunctive Relief Limited to Nevada Exclusivity
judgments.reason: Section 11(a)'s express Nevada remedy does not state that it is Licensee's exclusive remedy, and the issue merely seeks broader express protection.
